chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Umm Salama (may Allah have mercy on her) complained about her eyes during the month of Ramadan, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) instructed her to break the fast, and said: 'The evening meal (delayed until night) would destroy your eyes.'

key_terms.أُمُّ سَلَمَةَ: Umm Salama, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking fast due to eye illness in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the permissibility of breaking the fast for specific illnesses, using Umm Salama’s eye ailment as a precedent for medical exemption. The phrase 'ashā’ al-layl li-‘aynihi radiyyun' is interpreted by scholars as either the evening meal causing strain or the delay of breaking fast until night aggravating the condition, underscoring the principle that preserving health takes precedence over ritual observance. It serves as a foundational text in Shia fiqh for defining the limits of valid excuses for fasting.
